evidence.exact_quote: without mixing them into one untyped schema list. Tools owns web tool/routing

items.impact: Implementers can preserve tokens yet classify the same extract differently or resolve owner-document conflicts inconsistently, making compatibility behavior non-falsifiable.
items.statement: T-158 requires typed interpretation through Core rules and owner boundaries but supplies neither a token-to-type mapping nor a deterministic precedence rule and executable oracle for conflicts among those authorities.
items.title: Extract normalization lacks deterministic typing and precedence

evidence.exact_quote: - Tools can report browser, GUI, device/emulator, screenshot, log, launch, headless/headed, and native runner capabilities to Automated_Testing_System.

items.impact: Automated testing consumers may disagree about availability, freshness, degradation, and denial and can falsely present an optional or unavailable automation path as usable.
items.statement: T-159 enumerates discoverable automation capability classes and preference policy, but it does not define the typed capability record, availability/reason states, freshness semantics, or a consumer conformance oracle.
items.title: Automation capability reporting has no typed availability contract

evidence.exact_quote: - The same FileSafe, permissions, ignore, freshness, fallback, remote/cache/SSH, and no-leak policy envelope applies to every consumer.

items.impact: A shared ranker can still leak or return inconsistent candidates if consumers evaluate different policy generations or resolve FileSafe, permission, ignore, remote, cache, and SSH decisions in different orders.
items.statement: T-160 correctly mandates one shared DiscoveryService and one policy envelope, but omits policy snapshot identity, evaluation precedence, and consistency behavior across concurrent local, remote, cache, and SSH consumers.
items.title: Shared discovery policy envelope lacks snapshot consistency

evidence.exact_quote: - discover_paths requests/results use discovery-local enum values from the CV-291 canonical exact value registry.

items.impact: Enum spelling can remain exact while incompatible clients disagree about requiredness, nullability, cardinality, error/result exclusivity, and receipt correlation.
items.statement: T-161 names a rich request/result/receipt surface and delegates allowed values to CV-291, but does not establish field types, required versus optional fields, result/error invariants, or correlation and ordering rules for receipts.
items.title: discover_paths names fields without complete payload invariants

evidence.exact_quote: - content_candidate is never treated as verified text content.

items.impact: This boundary prevents ranked path hints from being misrepresented as verified content and preserves existing search, AST/LSP, test, and domain-verifier authority.
items.statement: T-162 provides an explicit and falsifiable authority boundary: DiscoveryService may identify content candidates, but exact content claims must be verified by the designated content-search or domain owner.
items.title: Path discovery versus content verification is explicit

evidence.exact_quote: - Superseded GUI discovery queries cancel within the configured cancellation target.

items.impact: Cancellation, fairness, concurrency, and backpressure implementations can all claim compliance without common numerical limits or race-safe state-transition tests, risking stale GUI results and starvation.
items.statement: T-163 requires deduplication, cancellation, fairness, bounded concurrency, and backpressure, but the cancellation target, resource caps, fairness rule, receipt ordering, and race or recovery oracles are unspecified.
items.title: Discovery scheduler guardrails lack measurable limits

evidence.exact_quote: - Do not omit uncertainty or limitations from bridge output when the image is ambiguous or low-confidence.

items.impact: Providers can implement incompatible bridge payloads and retention behavior, while users may receive unsourced, stale, over-retained, or misleading derived visual context despite the fail-closed prose.
items.statement: T-165 establishes automatic/manual routing and a strong never-guess rule, but leaves the request/output schema, route-selection precedence, reason-code enum, confidence representation, provenance binding, redaction, retention, revocation, and stale-artifact behavior undefined.
items.title: Vision bridge fails closed but lacks a complete typed contract

evidence.exact_quote: pm_gap_or_delta: 'Need explicit `ToolTurnSettlement` state machine for provider native turns: success, partial, truncated, malformed, nullable-content, redacted, retained, retryable, fatal.'

items.impact: Retries, retention, replay, and user-visible settlement can diverge because implementations have no canonical transition graph, terminal-state rules, idempotency rule, or atomic persistence boundary.
items.statement: T-167 names ToolTurnSettlement states and no-lossy-success behavior but does not define legal transitions, precedence among partial/truncated/redacted/retained states, terminality, retry budgets, idempotency, or atomic history admission.
items.title: ToolTurnSettlement is a state list rather than a state machine

evidence.exact_quote: P2-CACHEABLE-TOOL-OUTPUT-REFS (P2) is compiled as canonical Puppet Master intent for Hash-addressed cache refs for stable large tool outputs: Large stable outputs use refs with TTL/redaction; secrets are never cached; model-visible preview references complete retained output.

items.impact: Cache keys, redaction changes, permission changes, expiry, eviction, or offline access can expose stale or unauthorized data or leave previews pointing to unavailable retained output.
items.statement: T-168 requires hash-addressed refs, TTL/redaction, secret exclusion, and complete-output linkage, but omits ref schema, hash scope, tenant and permission binding, TTL start/expiry behavior, redaction-version invalidation, eviction recovery, and dereference failure oracles.
items.title: Cacheable tool output refs lack lifecycle and access semantics

evidence.exact_quote: - Partial streamed JSON/tool XML never becomes replayable assistant history.

items.impact: Malformed or duplicate calls may still cross the durable-history boundary during streaming races or crashes, and retry logic can create loops or double execution.
items.statement: T-169 defines the admission objective and rejected-record shape in prose, but not validation order, streaming finalization, duplicate-ID scope, transactional history admission, crash recovery, raw-redacted reference retention, or bounded loop policy.
items.title: Provider tool-turn admission lacks an atomic algorithm

evidence.exact_quote: - Default context never includes all full MCP schemas.

items.impact: Different callers can materialize different schema levels, overspend context, use stale permission-filtered slices, or omit instructions needed to invoke a selected capability safely.
items.statement: T-170 names L0 through L3 and several acceptance outcomes, but omits selection and escalation rules, cache-key inputs, permission-change invalidation atomicity, token thresholds, fallback when materialization fails, and conformance fixtures across capability families.
items.title: Progressive disclosure levels lack a materialization algorithm

evidence.exact_quote: - Approval UI displays the exact effective command form and quoting/escaping interpretation.

items.impact: Approval can describe a command differently from what executes, especially across POSIX shells, PowerShell, PTY input, environment expansion, and wrapper mutation, creating destructive-action risk.
items.statement: T-171 enumerates invocation kinds and requires exact approval display, but does not define platform-specific normalization and escaping, the canonical effective-command representation, environment and cwd validation, wrapper hashing, or when command mutation invalidates one-shot approval.
items.title: Command approval is not cryptographically bound to execution form

evidence.exact_quote: - Each session has ActiveToolNamespaceReceipt with configured, allowed, injected, visible_to_model, visible_to_ui, and startup status per tool namespace.

items.impact: UI chips, model schemas, mentions, and runtime tools can disagree during startup or refresh, falsely advertising a capability or silently withholding one without a reliable recovery path.
items.statement: T-172 requires ActiveToolNamespaceReceipt facts, but does not define their types, namespace identity, persistence and freshness, state precedence, atomic snapshot publication, refresh races, startup timeout, or reconciliation and rollback behavior.
items.title: Active tool namespace proof lacks schema and transition semantics

evidence.exact_quote: - Malformed JSON records parse error and raw captured bytes

items.impact: The system can either lose diagnostic evidence, leak sensitive raw bytes, or present a success-shaped result when parse and retention complete in different orders or partially fail.
items.statement: T-173 forbids fabricated output and requires parse-error capture, but does not define the gate order and atomic binding among parsing, raw-byte redaction, managed retention, ToolTurnSettlement, history admission, and UI presentation.
items.title: Tool truthfulness is not atomically bound to redacted retention

evidence.exact_quote: proposal_or_recommendation: Add ToolManagedOutputRef and retention-failure semantics

items.impact: Large results can be truncated, orphaned, over-retained, or reported successful after storage failure because neither the reference nor its failure and recovery lifecycle is executable canon.
items.statement: T-174 proposes ToolManagedOutputRef and a retention-failure blocker but supplies no ref fields, size threshold, storage authority, integrity check, redaction/access binding, lifetime, transactional settlement rule, cleanup, dereference failure, or recovery oracle.
items.title: ToolManagedOutputRef remains a proposal without a contract

evidence.exact_quote: pm_gap_or_delta: Need uniform ProgressHeartbeat, max silent interval, visible stalled state

items.impact: Long-running MCP, subagent, browser, and device work can hang indefinitely or be falsely marked stalled, while cancellation, timeout reset, and visible recovery differ by tool class.
items.statement: T-175 names ToolProgressHeartbeat, a max silent interval, and a visible stalled state but defines no payload, sequencing clock, interval and jitter bounds, progress semantics, liveness authority, stall transition, timeout-reset rule, cancellation race handling, terminal interaction, or recovery oracle.
items.title: Tool heartbeat has no protocol or stalled-state machine

segments.summary: Reviewed T-158 through T-163: the path-versus-content authority boundary is explicit, while extract normalization, capability reporting, shared policy snapshots, discover_paths payload invariants, and scheduler limits need deterministic contracts and oracles.
Reviewed T-165, T-167, and T-168: fail-closed vision, no-lossy tool settlement, and cached output refs are strong intents but lack complete wire, transition, access, and lifecycle contracts.
Reviewed T-169 through T-173: admission, materialization, command approval, namespace activation, and truthfulness have critical cross-stage atomicity, race, security, and falsifiability gaps.
Reviewed T-174 and T-175 plus the assigned repair addendum: managed output retention and heartbeat remain named requirements without executable ref, lifecycle, timing, or stalled-state protocols.

cross_document_questions: Which owner defines the typed DiscoveryRequest, DiscoveryResult, receipt, and policy-snapshot invariants referenced by Tools and CV-291?
Which storage and contract owner atomically binds ToolTurnSettlement, ProviderToolTurnAdmissionGate, ToolManagedOutputRef, raw-redacted evidence, and replayable history?
Which permissions and executor owner defines canonical effective-command normalization and binds approval to the exact executable form across POSIX, PowerShell, PTY, and TUI routes?
Which runtime owner publishes and reconciles ActiveToolNamespaceReceipt snapshots across model-visible schemas, UI chips, mentions, and actual injected tools?
Which executor, MCP, browser, device, and testing owner defines the shared ToolProgressHeartbeat timing and stalled-state protocol?
